title: Elevated response latency
summary: A downstream dependency, queue, or connection pool may be limiting request throughput.

steps.title: Compare endpoint and dependency timings
steps.rationale: Find where latency first increased before changing the application.

steps.title: Inspect connection-pool and queue saturation
steps.rationale: Check queue length, active connections, and timeouts against recent baseline.

steps.title: Review recent releases with the service owner
steps.rationale: If evidence links a release to the regression, have a human evaluate rollback safety.

title: Elevated application errors
summary: An application or dependency failure is increasing the request error rate.

steps.title: Group recent errors by signature
steps.rationale: Separate one failing dependency from broad application failures.

steps.title: Check dependency health and recent releases
steps.rationale: Correlate the first error with dependency availability and code changes.

steps.title: Ask the owner to review a mitigation plan
steps.rationale: Traffic changes, retries, and rollbacks require operational judgment.

title: Memory pressure
summary: Heap growth, a workload spike, or inefficient allocation may explain memory pressure.

steps.title: Compare heap growth and workload volume
steps.rationale: Distinguish sustained growth from a temporary batch or traffic spike.

steps.title: Review bounded memory diagnostics
steps.rationale: Use existing profiles and GC metrics; new profiling can affect performance.

steps.title: Have an owner evaluate capacity or restart options
steps.rationale: Restarting may lose state and must never be automatic.

title: CPU saturation
summary: Workload growth or a compute-heavy code path may be saturating the service.

steps.title: Compare CPU with request and job volume
steps.rationale: Determine whether load explains the saturation.

steps.title: Inspect existing hot-path profiles
steps.rationale: Identify a compute-heavy path without automatically attaching a profiler.

title: Failed health checks
summary: The endpoint is unavailable or its health contract is failing; the cause is not established.

steps.title: Verify the endpoint and network path
steps.rationale: A probe failure alone does not distinguish network, process, or health-contract failure.

steps.title: Inspect process and dependency health
steps.rationale: Collect evidence before proposing a restart or failover.

steps.title: Escalate to the service owner
steps.rationale: Availability mitigations can affect customer traffic and require human approval.
